area: Ownership: Storage contract split between WP-B and WP-C
location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetStore.swift:84-253 (16 `WP-C:` stubs) and :23 (`private let environment`); Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Staging/StoreStagingSink.swift:35+ (WP-B stubs); PROMPT.md §5 rows B/C and line 51 ("B, C, D, E in parallel"); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16
problem: PROMPT §5 runs WP-B and WP-C in parallel worktrees with separate write sets: B gets {FileSystem,Store,Index,Blobs,Lock,Snapshot} and C gets {Integrity,Cleanup,Eviction,Migration}. But almost every WP-C MUST is a fatalError stub inside Store/AssetStore.swift, which is in WP-B's directory and is an orchestrator contract file. That covers R-CLN-1..12, R-INT-3/4, R-STO-11 (migrateLegacy, adoptLegacyNow), R-CAR-8 leases and R-CLN-9 storageReport: evictionPlan, setRetentionScope, collectStaging, recordAccesses, acquireLease, releaseLease, setPinned, evictIfNeeded, collectGarbage, purge, reportUnreadable, verifyIntegrity, recordIntegrityFailure, storageReport, migrateLegacy and adoptLegacyNow. The actor's state is `private` to that file, and an actor extension in another file can neither add stored properties nor read private state. So WP-C cannot implement its requirements inside its own directories, and WP-B and WP-C would both edit one actor body, a guaranteed merge conflict that CLAUDE.md P2 calls an ownership bug. `Staging/` (StoreStagingSink, stubbed for WP-B) and `Layout/` are in nobody's write set. No document (ARCHITECTURE §1, DECISIONS) says how the actor is to be split.
fix: Before Stage 2, in the orchestrator's contract round: (a) move the 16 WP-C methods out of AssetStore.swift into `extension AssetStore` files under Cleanup/, Eviction/, Integrity/ and Migration/ (signatures and stubs unchanged). (b) Declare the shared store state in the contract as internal stored properties, or as one internal `StoreState` value with per-WP sub-structs. WP-B would own index, blob table, publishing and commit state. WP-C would own leases, pins, retention scope, integrity cursor and migration cursor. Extensions can then reach it. (c) Record in ARCHITECTURE §1/DECISIONS that `Staging/` and `Layout/` belong to WP-B. Alternative: sequence WP-C after WP-B is merged and grant it Store/AssetStore.swift explicitly.

area: Coherence: snapshot install rate (H-2, P-8, sync-2 S2-12 resolution)
problem: ARCHITECTURE §5, and the S2-12 resolution in §12.4, decide: "Bulk-work snapshot installs are rate-limited to ≤ 10 Hz (SyncTuning.snapshotInstallInterval); user-initiated commits install at once." The store is the only caller of SnapshotSink.install, and the contract does not let it do this. `publish(_:binding:expecting:)` takes no lane or urgency. StoreConfiguration has no install interval. AssetClient.init builds StoreConfiguration from location, storage and legacy only. `snapshotInstallInterval` is read by nothing (grep). WP-B is left with two choices. Installing on every publish costs an O(N) snapshot copy per commit, which is O(N²) store CPU over a 10,000-asset sync, plus 10,000 main-actor hops. Rate-limiting everything delays lookup for the page the user just opened.
fix: Add `snapshotInstallInterval` to StoreConfiguration, fed from `configuration.tuning` in AssetClient.init. Add an urgency input, e.g. `publish(_:binding:expecting:urgency: AssetPriority)` or `AssetStore.installSnapshotNow()`. Report the trailing install through `nextDeadline()`/`runDueWork()` (ADR-022). Name a regression test in §11.

location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetStore.swift (no such method; only :203 reportUnreadable and :215 recordIntegrityFailure); Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetRecord.swift (Residency.failed(FailureReason.notFound)); Sources/ZTronAssetModel/Events/EngineStates.swift:9-10; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:192
problem: Several places say a 404/410 is persisted. ARCHITECTURE §7.6 maps `permanentMissing` to `failed(.untilEntryChanges)` "(persisted, store)". RetryDisposition.untilEntryChanges is documented as "Persisted in the index: integrity quarantine or 404". Residency.failed(.notFound) and StoreError.assetFailed(_, .notFound) exist. But no AssetStore operation can record a not-found failure. WP-F can only keep it in memory, so every relaunch and every run requests the 404 assets again, which contradicts the documented decision. This is not a SPEC MUST, so it is non-blocking.
fix: Add `AssetStore.recordPermanentMissing(_ ids: [AssetID], identity: ContentIdentity) async throws(StoreError)`, or generalise to `recordFailure(_:identity:reason:)`. Clear it when the entry's content identity changes. Add a §11 test such as `R-NET-6: a 404 is not requested again until its manifest entry changes, across a relaunch`.

area: Configuration knobs not wired to their consumer
problem: Five settings never reach the code that needs them. (a) `LegacyMigrationPolicy.defaultsSuiteName` is never read. `AssetClient.init(configuration:environment: = .live())` builds `LiveLegacyDefaults(suiteName: nil)`. An app that sets a suite in the configuration therefore reads and removes `.standard`, and its real legacy stamp is neither migrated nor removed (R-STO-2/R-STO-11 for that configuration). (b) `AssetClientConfiguration.prefetchRadius` is unused; PrefetchWindowController uses its own default of 2. (c) `PlanningPolicy.evictionPermitted` has no source in StoragePolicy (R-SYN-11 "policy permitting"). (d) The store's documented cap check (ARCH §4.3 step 3, `StoreIntegrityFailure.oversize(limit:)`) has no `maxAssetBytes` in StoreConfiguration. (e) `DiagnosticReport.indexSchemaVersion` has no exported Storage constant.
fix: (a) Derive the live legacy defaults from the configuration, e.g. `environment: AssetEnvironment? = nil` resolving to `.live(legacyDefaultsSuiteName: configuration.legacy.defaultsSuiteName)`, or remove the field. (b) Default the controller's radius from `client.configuration.prefetchRadius`. (c) Add a StoragePolicy switch, or document that eviction is always permitted. (d) Add `limits` (or `maxAssetBytes`) to StoreConfiguration. (e) Export `StoreLayout.indexSchemaVersion`.

problem: Production never builds a background backend. The HTTPRemoteSource convenience init hardcodes `background: nil` and ignores `HTTPSourceConfiguration.background`. Nothing constructs BackgroundTransferCoordinator or LiveBackgroundSessionDriver. SessionDelegate holds only mode, staging and policy. It therefore has nowhere to deliver `SessionEvent`s: download tasks in a background session cannot use per-task mailboxes. It also has nowhere to deliver the `didBecomeInvalidWithError` signal that `ForegroundTransferBackend.invalidate()` must wait for (T2-04). My probe shows this is implementable without signature changes: an internal AsyncStream made with `makeStream` inside `init()`, a Sendable handle holding a URLSessionDataTask, and URLProtocol hop counting all typecheck clean at ios15 and macos12 with -warnings-as-errors. However, WP-D must edit contract bodies that are already implemented.
fix: State in ARCH §6.1 and §6.4 that WP-D owns these bodies. Have WP-D add an internal session-event stream to SessionDelegate, created in the existing init. Have the convenience init build the coordinator over LiveBackgroundSessionDriver when `.enabled`.

location: Sources/ZTronAssetTestSupport/RecordingFakes.swift (FakeRemoteSource scripting API, FakeTransferStep.stage(Data)); Tests/ZTronAssetKitBenchmarks/QualityBudgets.swift:61 (standalone BudgetsBenchmarks); PROMPT.md §5 (benchmarks target unowned)
problem: Three gaps. (a) FakeRemoteSource has no way to script `reattachedTransfers()`, which the H-6 engine tests need (R-NET-3 adoption from staging, R-CLN-3 survival through launch GC). (b) `.stage(Data)` is the only way to produce bytes, so P-7's 1 GiB catalog must sit in RAM up front, which complicates "delta must not grow with catalog size". (c) The S2-14 resolution says benchmarks run serialized under one parent suite, but the contract declares no parent suite. Seven WPs will add files to an unowned benchmarks target, and independent top-level suites run concurrently, contaminating P-1, P-6, P-9 and P-12.
fix: WP-H adds `scriptReattached(_:)` and a seeded `.stageGenerated(seed:byteCount:)` step. The orchestrator declares `@Suite(.serialized) struct ZTronAssetKitBenchmarks {}` (name contains "Benchmarks") and requires each WP's benchmarks to be nested `extension` suites in per-WP files.

problem: Five `await`s inside TestSupport actors have no `// REENTRANCY:` comment. C3 applies to every actor, and ARCH §10 says "A new await without a row is a review failure". For example, SteppedBlockingExecutor.run mutates `completed` after resuming. The ledger covers only AssetStore and SyncEngine.
fix: Add REENTRANCY comments stating what is re-validated (mostly nothing, because each await is a terminal wait), or add a TestSupport section to ARCH §10.

location: Sources/ZTronAssetModel/Environment/AssetLog.swift:94-98; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §14 bullet 2 ("the .background delegate paths driven through a foreground session")
problem: Two test paths would write outside the repository. (a) `AssetLog.emit` always writes to os.Logger, and no seam routes lines only to the LogTap. Once implementations log at .info or above, every test that exercises those paths will persist lines into the system's unified-log store. (b) If WP-D drives the background delegate paths with real download tasks, CFNetwork writes `CFNetworkDownload_*.tmp` files under DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR (the T2-01 defect), even when the file is then moved into staging.
fix: Add a log-sink seam, e.g. a `LogSink` whose live conformer is os.Logger and which tests replace with a tap-only sink. Specify that background-delegate tests call the delegate methods directly with an unresumed task and a location file inside the repository, never with real download tasks.
